payload.feature: tui graph: the selection box gets continuous walls. Operator ruling (2026-08-31), superseding the walls-skip-the-rail-row choice from the box-meets-rail slice (PR #66) and, where they conflict, the 'rail is one unbroken line' pin: the box around the selected phase still reads as misaligned because its sides are gap-toothed — a corner floats above a connector dash with a hole where the rail passes (measured: the done box's ╭ sits over the connector's dash run with nothing beneath it, and the verify box's corners sit over dashes on both sides). The fix is the inverse ruling: WALLS ARE CONTINUOUS. Each side of the dashed selection box is drawn on EVERY row from the top corner to the bottom corner, including the rail row — ─┆─ reads as the rail meeting a fence post, which looks deliberate; a hovering corner over track does not. Constraints: a wall glyph must never overwrite an arrowhead (ᐳ) or any node glyph (the mark/ramp glyphs) — when a computed wall column lands on one, shift that wall outward to the nearest column whose rail-row cell is a dash or a space; the two walls remain symmetric around the box contents where the shift allows; corners keep their rounded dashed vocabulary (╭ ╮ ╰ ╯ ╌ ┆); the snug-per-phase envelope from PR #66 (plain phase snug, fork spans its lanes) is untouched; plan stays pure integer geometry, paint keeps no clipping branch, all glyphs pass the sanitized constructors, elision marks keep column 0 and the last column, the rail keys are untouched. Update the superseded pins and their tests to the new ruling — never fake an old pin passing. Tests must pin: every box side is gapless (a wall glyph on every row between its corners, rail row included); no wall glyph on ᐳ or a node glyph in any plan over runs with plain phases, wide baseline labels (ship ×2), and forks; the outward shift when a wall would land on a head; and the snug/fork envelopes unchanged. CI enforces exact coverage — keep the gate green.

inputs.goal: selection_box in crates/forge-cli/src/tui.rs draws its walls on every row including the rail row (no more skip), with an outward shift off arrowhead/node-glyph columns; supersedes PR #66's walls-skip-the-rail-row pin and the affected test in tui/tests.rs

result.notes: Framed the box-walls-continuous slice: make the selection box's dashed sides gapless (wall glyph on every row, rail row included), add an outward-shift-off-a-head rule for the rail row only, and update the now-superseded PR #66 pin (no_wall_of_the_selection_box_stands_on_an_arrowhead's 'rail passes through both walls' assertion) plus its stale comments. Pure paint()-side change in tui.rs; no plan() geometry change, no contract/policy/reference touch.

inputs.coverage: crates/forge-cli/src/tui.rs at 100% lines / 100% branches / 100% functions under cargo +nightly llvm-cov --branch; the full scripts/coverage-exact.sh gate could not be run in this seat (bash approval denied for the script), so the per-file check stands in for it

result.notes: selection_box now draws each side on every row from top corner to bottom corner, rail row included — the `if row == plan.rail_row { continue; }` skip is gone. A new `track()` helper reads the already-painted `cells` at a rail-row column and answers whether it is the rail's own dash or blank ground; each wall independently searches outward from its padded column (`seg.x0 - BOX_PAD` / `seg.x1 + BOX_PAD`) to the nearest such column, bounded by columns 1 and width-2 so the elision marks keep theirs, falling back to the padded column — a bounded search over painted cells, no clipping branch, plan geometry untouched. Comments above selection_box and in paint that described the skip as deliberate now describe the 2026-08-31 ruling and its supersession of #66 and, where they conflict, the 'rail is one unbroken line' pin. Superseded tests were rewritten, not left vacuous: no_wall_of_the_selection_box_stands_on_an_arrowhead lost its `row == plan.rail_row ||` excuse and its closing assertion now pins that both walls carry `┆` on the rail row and that the rail runs INTO them from outside; every_connector_between_two_phases_is_the_same_length now asserts a wall really does cross a connector and reads it back as the dash it replaced (rhythm, not length, is its subject). New tests: every_side_of_the_selection_box_is_drawn_without_a_gap (corners plus `┆` on every row between, over the plain phase, the wide `ship ×2` label and the fork, asserting the rail row is strictly inside); no_wall_of_the_selection_box_is_drawn_over_a_head_or_a_node (each plan painted twice, with and without selection — no cell that held `ᐳ` or a node/spine glyph comes back wearing box); a_wall_steps_outward_off_a_head_rather_than_stand_on_it (no-shift baseline, one head, two heads, a node glyph on the previous segment, and the right wall shifting alone over blank ground — both sides of the shift branch and both operands of the track test). The snug/fork envelope tests pass unchanged. cargo fmt and clippy --all-targets -D warnings are clean.
